title: How micro-dramas could revolutionise our viewing habits
titleChinese: 微短剧如何重塑我们的观影习惯
paragraphs: Streaming video platforms have given filmmakers massive budgets and allowed them to make creative and artistic films and series free of the restrictions of cinema or broadcast time slots. But, maybe, just maybe, not everyone wants a three-hour long work of creative genius. Minute-long micro-dramas are taking the entertainment market by storm.

Perhaps most people are looking for something that they can squeeze into their everyday life. Micro-dramas cater perfectly for this need. It's not just that you can watch them on your phone, they're made for it. They're shot in vertical format, so you don't even have to turn your phone round to start watching. Series are split into as many as a hundred short episodes, so they can fit into any spare downtime that you have.

For this to work, it needs a new kind of programme. US tech company Quibi tried to use traditional Hollywood stars, and collapsed in less than a year, taking $1.75 billion dollars' worth of investment with it. Chinese start-up companies took a different approach, focusing on low-cost production and using analytics data and AI analysis to identify exactly what gets the audience to start watching, and then how to make the next episode feel unmissable.

Billionaires, breakups and bust-ups: those are the key themes that get the audience watching. There isn't much room for nuance or slow-build character development in a micro-drama, but what is needed is drama. Rather than a subscription model, monetisation in the world of micro-dramas is often based on a freemium model. You can see enough episodes to get you hooked for free. But you need to buy credits to find out how the story ends. This means that dramatic cliffhangers are a commercial tool.

These dramas are increasing in popularity around the world. There is also great potential to make money from advertising as audiences are highly engaged. After China, the US has become the biggest micro-drama market. Could it be that soon most of the drama we watch is on our phones in those minutes we find between our other daily tasks?
chineseParagraphs: 流媒体视频平台为电影制作人提供了巨额预算，使他们能够创作出不受影院或播出时段限制的创意艺术电影和剧集。但是，也许，只是也许，并不是每个人都想看长达三小时的创意天才之作。时长仅一分钟的微短剧正风靡娱乐市场。
也许大多数人都在寻找能融入日常生活的消遣。微短剧完美地迎合了这种需求。这可不仅仅是你可以在手机上观看，实际上它们就是为此而生的。它们采用竖屏格式拍摄，所以你甚至不需要转动手机就可以开始观看。剧集被分成多达上百集，可以填充你拥有的任何空闲时间。
要实现这一点，需要一种新型节目。美国科技公司Quibi曾尝试使用传统好莱坞明星，但不到一年就倒闭了，损失了17.5亿美元的投资。中国的初创公司们采取了不同的方法，专注于低成本制作，并利用分析数据和人工智能分析来准确识别是什么让观众开始观看，以及如何让下一集感觉不容错过。
亿万富翁、分手和争吵：这些是吸引观众观看的关键主题。微短剧中几乎没有空间容纳细微变化或缓慢的角色发展，但需要的是戏剧冲突。微短剧的变现模式通常不是订阅制，而是基于“免费增值”模式。你可以免费观看足够多的剧集以被吸引。但你需要购买金币才能知道故事的结局。这意味着戏剧性的悬念是一种商业工具。
这些短剧在全球越来越受欢迎。由于观众参与度很高，广告也带来了巨大的盈利潜力。继中国之后，美国已成为最大的微短剧市场。会不会很快，我们看的大部分剧都是在手机上，在我们其他日常任务之间能找到的那些时间里呢？

vocabulary.entry: micro-drama /ˈmaɪkrəʊ ˌdrɑːmə/ n. 微短剧（新造词）
vocabulary.example: Micro-dramas are becoming increasingly popular on social media platforms.
vocabulary.translation: 微短剧在社交媒体平台上越来越受欢迎。

vocabulary.entry: streaming /ˈstriːmɪŋ/ n. 流媒体播放（专业术语）
vocabulary.example: Streaming has changed the way we watch TV.
vocabulary.translation: 流媒体改变了我们看电视的方式。

vocabulary.entry: restriction /rɪˈstrɪkʃn/ n. 限制，约束（书面语）
vocabulary.example: There are strict restrictions on smoking in public places.
vocabulary.translation: 公共场所吸烟有严格限制。

vocabulary.entry: time slot /ˈtaɪm slɒt/ n. 播出时段（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: The show has a prime-time time slot on Friday nights.
vocabulary.translation: 该节目在周五晚上有一个黄金时段播出。

vocabulary.entry: squeeze /skwiːz/ v. 挤压，塞进（口语）
vocabulary.example: Can you squeeze another person into the car?
vocabulary.translation: 你能再往车里塞一个人吗？

vocabulary.definition: 迎合，满足需要（固定表达）
vocabulary.entry: cater for /ˈkeɪtə fɔː(r)/ phr. v. 迎合，满足需要（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: The hotel caters for all kinds of guests.
vocabulary.translation: 这家酒店迎合各种客人的需求。

vocabulary.entry: vertical format /ˈvɜːtɪkl ˈfɔːmæt/ n. 竖屏格式（专业术语）
vocabulary.example: Vertical format videos are designed for mobile viewing.
vocabulary.translation: 竖屏格式视频是为手机观看而设计的。

vocabulary.entry: episode /ˈepɪsəʊd/ n. （电视剧的）一集
vocabulary.example: The next episode airs on Friday.
vocabulary.translation: 下一集在周五播出。

vocabulary.entry: downtime /ˈdaʊntaɪm/ n. 休息时间，停工时间
vocabulary.example: Everyone needs a bit of downtime to relax.
vocabulary.translation: 每个人都需要一点休息时间来放松。

vocabulary.entry: collapsed /kəˈlæpst/ v. 倒塌，崩溃（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The company collapsed after the financial crisis.
vocabulary.translation: 公司在金融危机后倒闭了。

vocabulary.entry: start-up /ˈstɑːt ʌp/ n. 初创公司（书面语）
vocabulary.example: She works for a tech start-up in London.
vocabulary.translation: 她在伦敦一家科技初创公司工作。

vocabulary.entry: analytics data /ˌænəˈlɪtɪks ˈdeɪtə/ n. 分析数据（专业术语）
vocabulary.example: Analytics data helps companies understand customer behaviour.
vocabulary.translation: 分析数据帮助公司了解客户行为。

vocabulary.entry: unmissable /ʌnˈmɪsəbl/ adj. 不容错过的（口语）
vocabulary.example: The final episode of the series is unmissable.
vocabulary.translation: 这部系列剧的最后一集不容错过。

vocabulary.entry: bust-up /ˈbʌst ʌp/ n. 争吵，争执（英式口语）
vocabulary.example: They had a major bust-up over money.
vocabulary.translation: 他们因为钱大吵了一架。

vocabulary.entry: nuance /ˈnjuːɑːns/ n. 细微差别（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The actor’s performance captured every nuance of the character.
vocabulary.translation: 这位演员的表演捕捉到了角色的每一个细微之处。

vocabulary.entry: subscription model /səbˈskrɪpʃn ˈmɒdl/ n. 订阅模式（专业术语）
vocabulary.example: Many streaming services use a subscription model.
vocabulary.translation: 许多流媒体服务使用订阅模式。

vocabulary.definition: 变现，货币化（专业术语，书面语）
vocabulary.entry: monetisation /ˌmʌnɪtaɪˈzeɪʃn/ n. 变现，货币化（专业术语，书面语）
vocabulary.example: The monetisation of online content is a key challenge for creators.
vocabulary.translation: 在线内容的变现是创作者面临的关键挑战。

vocabulary.definition: 免费增值模式（专业术语）
vocabulary.entry: freemium /ˈfriːmiəm/ n. 免费增值模式（专业术语）
vocabulary.example: The app uses a freemium model with basic free features and premium upgrades.
vocabulary.translation: 这款应用采用免费增值模式，提供基本免费功能和付费升级。

vocabulary.entry: hooked /hʊkt/ adj. 上瘾的，入迷的（口语）
vocabulary.example: I'm completely hooked on this new TV show.
vocabulary.translation: 我完全迷上了这部新电视剧。

vocabulary.definition: 信用，金币（此处为应用内虚拟货币）
vocabulary.entry: credit /ˈkredɪt/ n. 信用，金币（此处为应用内虚拟货币）
vocabulary.example: You need to buy credits to unlock premium features.
vocabulary.translation: 你需要购买金币才能解锁高级功能。

vocabulary.definition: 悬念，扣人心弦的局面（影视术语）
vocabulary.entry: cliffhanger /ˈklɪfhæŋə(r)/ n. 悬念，扣人心弦的局面（影视术语）
vocabulary.example: The episode ended with a cliffhanger.
vocabulary.translation: 这一集以悬念结尾。

vocabulary.entry: commercial tool /kəˈmɜːʃl tuːl/ n. 商业工具（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: Cliffhangers are often used as a commercial tool to keep viewers coming back.
vocabulary.translation: 悬念常被用作商业工具来让观众持续关注。

vocabulary.entry: potential /pəˈtenʃl/ n. 潜力，潜能（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The new product has great sales potential.
vocabulary.translation: 这款新产品有很大的销售潜力。

vocabulary.entry: engaged /ɪnˈɡeɪdʒd/ adj. 投入的，参与的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The audience was fully engaged throughout the performance.
vocabulary.translation: 观众在整个表演过程中都非常投入。

vocabulary.entry: market /ˈmɑːkɪt/ n. 市场
vocabulary.example: The company is expanding into new markets.
vocabulary.translation: 公司正在扩展到新市场。
